#108143. Breaking: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

📅 06 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 33m • 📚 Deep Dive (6626 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

📅 06 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 33 min read (6626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~33 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.
  • The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his newly introduced club Chelsea in the lead.
  • That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his newly introduced club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

It has been revealed that instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

It has been revealed that as for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

Sources indicate that this was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

According to recent reports, arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be noted that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

According to recent reports, “Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

It has been revealed that in the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

Recent findings suggest that for the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

In a recent development, chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

According to recent reports, ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0.

It has been revealed that “I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”.

It has been revealed that “It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We indicated our quality today. The result reflected that.”.

On his relationship with Kai Havertz:.

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”.

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”.

It has been revealed that it is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

In a recent development, it is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

In a recent development, “This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. According to recent reports, A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. So far this season, Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in both league games. Gyokeres, by contrast, has played zero minutes.

Industry observers note that mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

According to recent reports, “We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”.

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

Industry observers note that two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta noted. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”.

According to recent reports, chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”.

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

Tech Report: Dual passports glitch continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

Industry observers note that the Dutch football association KNVB launched an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser said it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

It has been revealed that “Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius noted he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

“I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that claims I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

Né à Firminy, conseiller municipal de Saint-Etienne (depuis 8 mois) et parlementaire le plus investi dans le soutien aux ultras stéphanois (il avait été un des premiers signataires de notre pétition lancée le printemps 2025 et ayant recueilli plus de 5 800 signatures), le député PS ligérien Pierrick Courbon (41 ans) a posté cet après-midi le message suivant sur son compte Instagram.

In a recent development, "Ce qui s'est passé à Reims est inacceptable ! Les supporters ne sont pas des sous-citoyens, encore moins du bétail. Je saisis le Ministre de l'Intérieur. Malgré trois décisions de justice confirmant l'absence d'interdiction d'accès au stade tout comme les déplacements en autocars, les supporters stéphanois ont été interpellés à proximité du stade Auguste-Delaune, et contraints de faire demi-tour sous escorte policière. Il est indéniable que des erreurs ont été commises par les services de l'Etat, et qu'un contournement des décisions de justice a eu lieu.

In a recent development, les supporters ne sont pas des sous-citoyens. Pourtant, depuis de nombreuses années, le supportérisme est un laboratoire commode de mesures sécuritaires et liberticides, qui ne seraient toélérées dans un autre pan de la société. Comme je m'y suis engagé dès samedi, je viens d'alerter Laurent Nunez pour demander des réponses et des explications. La gestion des supporters en France est catastrophique. Je continuerai de les défendre car l'enjeu dépasse le simple cadre sportif.".

Roberto De Zerbi defends Mykhailo Mudryk after on-loan star angered Spurs fans with interview gaffes - including admitting he wanted to join Arsenal

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Mykhailo Mudryk is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.
  • Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 20 November 2026.

Mykhailo Mudryk is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.

Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.

He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'.

And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission.

'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' mentioned Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London.

'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a substantial club, like the other clubs, not less at all.'.

Mykhailo Mudryk admitted he joined Tottenham to regain fitness before returning to Chelsea, while also stating he had wanted to sign for Arsenal in 2023 before his transfer to the Blues.

Roberto De Zerbi acknowledged Tottenham fans' views on Mudryk's comments, but insisted the winger has 'suffered a lot' following his doping ban.

Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition.

'He has no responsibility in this part,' remarked De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a massive chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play.

'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.'.

Sources indicate that mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return.

'The plan was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' mentioned De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.'.

James Maddison's limited involvement for Tottenham relates to a niggling hip injury dating back to pre-season.

Maddison has been an unused sub in two Spurs games since limping off when the problem flared up at Chelsea, on his second start of the season and his second start in six days.

Roberto De Zerbi confirmed ahead of Saturday's game against Ipswich that it had been the same problem which dogged Maddison through the summer as he fought back from a serious knee injury.

The Spurs boss revealed how his physical condition had suffered from not training regularly and reminded the 29-year-old England midfielder he could only make an impact in the Premier League in peak condition.

De Zerbi confirmed James Maddison is available to face Ipswich but stressed the midfielder needs to push himself to reach his peak physical condition.

Recent findings suggest that 'It is not a massive injury, but he was not able to work,' explained De Zerbi. 'He had a problem with his hip. The same as preseason. It's not a big problem but if you don't work consistently you lose the physical condition and to play in this level of competition you have to stay in the top physical condition.'.

Maddison, who turns 30 on Monday, missed most of last season with a cruciate knee injury and has played only 195 minutes this season. His return was further complicated by a shoulder injury after coming on at Brentford on the opening game of the season.

It has been revealed that 'He is still young, 29 years is not old,' stated De Zerbi. 'He has to push and demand of himself the top in terms of physical condition, because if he is 80 or 90 per cent of his physical condition he makes the difference for us, he changes the games.'.

Maddison and Destiny Udogie have both trained fully through the international break and are available to face Ipswich.

'He worked very well from the Wednesday after Leeds,' stated De Zerbi. 'From Chelsea to the Leeds game, he worked just three times on the pitch at the training ground.

It has been revealed that 'If you don't work during the week you risk injury and lose the normal physical condition you need to play Premier League. The same for Udogie. When they work and are fit to work, they have many chances to play, especially Maddison because a special player.'.

Industry observers note that maddison's first start of the season came against Coventry when he scored the opener and inspired Spurs to their first win. He barely trained but started again in the win at Chelsea five days later, where he broke down early in the second half and was replaced by Conor Gallagher.

Sources indicate that de Zerbi made it clear there were no problems connected to Maddison being pictured out at a pub in Coventry after the defeat at Leeds. It was the last game before the international break and the first of three days off.

Recent findings suggest that 'I am angry because next time he has to invite me,' joked the Spurs boss and he added: 'I am happy. I know when my players work well. If they are serious on the pitch, off the pitch they can do what they want. I'm not a policeman.

'James is top professional, top guy, top player. The private life is not our problem if they work well and they are serious, and give their best for the club, the shirt and the fans, and he is perfect when it comes to that.'.

Sources indicate that les U15 de Benjamin Petit, après leur précieuse victoire d'il y a deux semaines contre Villefranche (1-0) se déplaçaient cet après-midi sur le terrain de l'AS Saint-Priest, qui n'est jamais un adversaire facile. Auparavant, dans la semaine, mercredi, à Cruas, ils s'étaient mesurés à l'Olympique de Marseille, leader de la poule Méditerranée, et qui, en match amical, a largement battu bon nombre d'équipes de renom. Les jeunes Verts avaient mieux fait que se défendre, ne s'inclinant que sur le score de 2 à 1. Revenons-en au match d'aujourd'hui pour dire que la victoire est revenue en toute logique aux jeunes Verts sur le score de 2 à 1, une victoire qui va leur permettre d'engranger des points et....de la confiance.

Recent findings suggest that ce sont les Sanpriods qui ont ouvert la marque, contre le cours du jeu, à la 19ème minute sur une approximation défensive. Mais les Verts réagissaient immédiatement et, deux minutes plus tard, à la 21ème, Kaïs Boukerma, sur une passe de Charly Davignon, de l'entrée de la surface, plaçait une frappe au ras du poteau pour l'égalisation. Un quart d'heure plus tard, à la 36ème, Hugo Bastide, qui opérait aujourd'hui en défense centrale, récupérait fort à propos un 2ème ballon sur un corner pour donner l'avantage aux Verts. Ce fut difficile après le repos, car Saint-Priest mettait la pression pour revenir au score. Mais les Verts faisaient preuve de solidarité et de rigueur défensive pour conserver cet avantage de 2 à 1.A noter la victoire des U14 sur le score de 8 à 1. Nous reviendrons ultérieurement sur la belle saison de cette équipe.

La composition : Clapeyron - Bergougnoux, Wojcik, Bastide, Uneau - Boukerma, Lebreton (L.La Rosa, 45ème), M.La Rosa (Linganzi Koumba, 40ème) - Fernandes (Moutae, 50ème), Bangoura, Davignon.

La réaction de Benjamin Petit : "Nous avons fait une bonne première mi-temps, même si nous avons un peu manqué de tranchant dans le domaine offensif. Il n'a pas manqué grand chose sur plusieurs situations intéressantes. C'est là un axe de progrès bien identifié que d'aller chercher cette réussite offensive. J'ai apprécié le fait que les garçons soient restés sereins après l'ouverture du score par Saint-Priest. Cela leur a permis de revenir rapidement et de passer devant avant la pause. Par contre, la deuxième mi-temps a été plus compliquée. Saint-Priest nous a mis la pression et nous avons eu plus de mal à construire et à progresser à l'intérieur du jeu. Mais nous avons fait preuve de caractère, de rigueur défensive et cela nous a permis de conserver le résultat.".

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

According to recent reports, referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst stated wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

Recent findings suggest that one flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst stated. “What do you do about that?”.

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente stated the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

In a recent development, “This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

According to recent reports, van Bronckhorst remarked he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

Industry observers note that “Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vous avez pu suivre cette rencontre en direct sur notre forum grâce à notre envoyé spécial MachuPicchu42 : les U17 ont concédé un match nul et vierge à la mi-journée face au Cavigal de Nice au Stade Georges Bereta du Centre Robert Herbin.

Dominateurs jusqu'à l'entame du dernier quart d'heure, les Verts ont eu deux grosses occasions en première période. Sur la première, le portier niçois a repoussé le tir à bout portant de Naël Dani. Sur la seconde, un défenseur visiteur a repoussé sur sa ligne une tête d'Isaak Seydi (photo).

En deuxième mi-temps, Lohoré Gobé a eu à son tour une belle opportunité d'ouvrir le score mais sa tentative a été déjouée par le gardien azuréen. Isaak Seydi a de nouveau eu une occase de la tête, hélas non cadrée. Izaya Kimpioka a raté un face à face en tirant à côté. Les visteurs se sont enhardis lors de 20 dernières minutes pas très bien maîtrisées par les Stéphanois mais Andra Laugier n'aura eu aucun arrêt à faire de toute la rencontre.

L'ASSE a perdu sa 5e place au profit de son ex-club partenaire Saint-Priest, qui a cartonné 6-1 le Gazelec Ajaccio (avant-dernier), prochain adversaire des Verts (dimanche prochain en Corse).

La compo : Laugier - Tiambo (Balta, 33') - Mnemoi, Dagbo, Bufferne - Demassieux, Mendy (Thibaudat, 77'), Gobé - Seydi, Kimpioka, Dani (Aytone, 70').

Industry observers note that la réaction de David Le Moal : "On a eu la mainmise sur le match jusqu'au dernier quart d'heure. On a eu pas mal d'occasions, c'est dommage qu'on n'ait pas réussi à les convertir. En première période, on a eu du mal à passer l'adversaire dans le coeur du jeu donc on s'est évertué à contourner le bloc assez bas du Cavigal. On a eu plein de situations de centres mais on a manqué de réalisme dans le dernier geste ou dans l'avant-dernier geste. On a eu plusieurs occasions assez nettes en première période comme en seconde. Je n'ai pas trop compris pourquoi on a reculé lors du dernier quart d'heure, nos adversaires ont eu quelques opportunités en fin de match. Je suis un peu déçu qu'on n'ait pas réussi à marquer mais je suis assez content des vrais gestes défensifs et de la discipline tactique, on a laissé très peu de situations à l'adversaire.".

Industry News: Celtic boss O'Neill seeks Europa League stand-in as Baur set for lengthy spell on the sidelines

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (730 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Martin O'Neill will weigh up replacing Mika Baur in the Europa League squad after the midfielder was ruled out for up to 10 weeks with an ankle injury.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

Martin O'Neill will weigh up replacing Mika Baur in the Europa League squad after the midfielder was ruled out for up to 10 weeks with an ankle injury.

The German hobbled off late on in Celtic's win over Kilmarnock almost a fortnight ago with a scan subsequently revealing that he sustained ligament damage.

One of the Parkhead side's star men since signing from Paderborn in the summer, Baur's absence is a major blow for O'Neill ahead of a defining period in the season.

While the manager will look to the likes of Oliver Sorensen and Joel van den Berg to step up domestically, he will also consider using a UEFA rule to make a change to his European squad ahead of Thursday's match away to Torreense in Portugal.

The rule allows clubs to make an alteration to the squad they submitted for the group stage if the injury is expected to sideline the player for more than 60 days from when it occurred.

Van den Berg, Jota, Landon Emenalo and Shim Mheuka weren't on the original 25-man list so would be options to be drafted in.

German midfielder Mika Baur could miss up to 10 weeks of action after injuring his ankle.

'I would definitely check with the medical staff and Mika, for a start,' mentioned O'Neill.

'And speaking to him yesterday, he's really upbeat about it. Obviously, he will have that boot on for a few weeks.

In a recent development, 'I suppose deep down, if it was, let's say, 10 weeks, that's taking you right through to the end of January. I can't see us seeing him in the next six weeks.'.

Baur's form following his £4.5million move has been good enough for him to win his first full cap for Germany after being called up by fresh manager Jurgen Klopp.

In a recent development, 'He was doing great for us,' added O'Neill. 'It is a blow. And it seemed so innocuous at the time.

'I thought that he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he'd landed on. It's just gone over. It's a real shame. He was playing great for us.

'There's things that he can't do for a while.'.

O'Neill revealed that Benjamin Nygren is also an injury doubt for Saturday's match with St Mirren.

In a recent development, 'He didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning,' he explained. 'He's got a sore heel. He missed out the second game in Sweden's run.

'He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks, so we'll see how he is tomorrow.'.

19-year-old summer signing Joel van den Berg could make his first Celtic outing this weekend.

Van den Berg hasn't played for the first team since joining from PSV Eindhoven for £3.4m in the summer with an injury impeding his progress.

But the 19-year-old could be in line for his first-team debut against the Buddies.

It has been revealed that 'I had a little chat to him,' stated O'Neill. 'He trained this morning, he didn't train yesterday. We played a bounce game during the week, Tuesday against St Johnstone.

'He played in that game, came off and he was definitely limping for a while. He had a couple of days' treatment.

'In the overall scheme of things, whether it's tomorrow or in the next week or two, I'd hope to see him make his mark.

'As I said to him yesterday, "When you get in, it's really up to you".'.

O'Neill anticipates a stern test from a St Mirren side who often have not picked up the positive results their performances have merited under Craig McLeish.

'The overall job he's done has been terrific, really terrific,' stated the Celtic manager.

'They're having a wee tough time at this minute, obviously, with results, but his overall contributions, I'd say it's been excellent.

'There are some really fine coaches in Scotland, genuinely, and I don't want to sound patronising or sycophantic, but there are.

'We were up against one two weeks ago against Kilmarnock [Neil McCann], so I've got a lot of time for those boys who are coming through and who, to my mind, are every bit as good of coaches as quite a number down south.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

According to recent reports, their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

Recent findings suggest that but here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

“Brilliant technique,” remarked David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Industry observers note that benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Industry observers note that yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

Sources indicate that “We’re bitterly disappointed,” mentioned Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

It has been revealed that but clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their latest sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

Industry observers note that this is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

Industry observers note that united dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

Industry observers note that when Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

It has been revealed that his substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

It has been revealed that "That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia.

Sources indicate that “I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”.

Industry observers note that they did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

It has been revealed that as Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq.

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

Recent findings suggest that it’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

Industry observers note that I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

In a recent development, "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”.

Recent findings suggest that george finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Sources indicate that as Dominic indicates, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

In a recent development, speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Noham Akil, buteur après son entrée en jeu.

According to recent reports, ayant mis fin le week-end dernier à une série de 5 défaites consécutives, les U19 de Frédéric Dugand, victorieux à domicile du Cap d’Ail (2-1) se déplaçaient à Nice ce dimanche, pour y affronter le très bon club formateur du Cavigal. Une victoire sur la Côte d’Azur permettait aux jeunes Verts de rejoindre son adversaire au classement (13 points).

Sous une légère pluie, dans un stade Bob Rémond, du nom du formateur Niçois, aussi appelé « père spirituel de Robert Herbin », les Stéphanois, réduits à 10 et menés au score ont été cherché l’égalisation en toute fin de rencontre (1-1).

Industry observers note that en première période les Verts, avec notamment Noa Moulin, habituellement aligné en réserve, sont bien en place et disciplinés mais restent un peu timides dans leurs actions pour espérer peser davantage sur la rencontre. A la 23ème minute, consécutivement à un corner adverse mal repoussé, le ballon arrive au second poteau, est remis dans la surface verte et repris par un niçois qui vient tromper Mael Massé pour l’ouverture du score. (Cavigal Nice 1 - ASSE 0 ; mi-temps).

Au retour des vestiaires, les Stéphanois plus entreprenants vont chercher l’adversaire plus haut. Progressivement, les contres deviennent verts et la confiance revient. Pourtant à l’heure de jeu, la situation se complique, Tidiane Vibert est exclu pour un geste d’humeur et laisse ses coéquipiers en infériorité numérique. Touchés, mais pas coulés, les Stéphanois, sous l’impulsion notamment de l’entrant Medhy Lutin Zidee à la 56ème continuent à faire bloc et à jouer les coups à fond. Leurs efforts vont être récompensés, à la 84ème minute,  Maxime Lengué Lenou trouve Noham Akil (entré quelques minutes plus tôt) qui du pied droit vient ajuster le portier azuréen. Les Verts sont décomplexés et tiennent ce point précieux qui les voit enchainer une seconde rencontre consécutive sans perdre.

(Cavigal Nice 1 - ASSE 1 ; score final).

Après ce partage des points, les Stéphanois auront la semaine prochaine l’occasion de poursuivre leur série dans leur quête de points pour assurer le maintien avec la réception du  Gazelec Ajaccio, auteur d’un nul aujourd’hui face à Balma (1-1) et comptant le même nombre de points que les Verts, mais un match en moins..

La Composition : Massé  – Lengi (Assoumani 81ème),  E.Mnemoi, N.Mouton, Jolivet, Lengue Lenou– Vibert, Thouilleux (Akil 76ème), Moulin (Gary 56ème), Marliac(Lutin Zidee 56ème) - Zibi.

According to recent reports, la réaction de Frédéric Dugand : « Je suis satisfait du résultat, de la capacité du groupe à avoir respecté le plan de jeu décidé, un peu plus prudent qu’à l’habitude. On fait une bonne seconde période, les joueurs ont eu du répondant. J’ai vu un groupe « habité »des joueurs qui se sont parlé et qui ont été acteurs du match. Le groupe se transforme, il faut capitaliser sur cette attitude, tâcher maintenant d’avoir cette mentalité dès le coup d’envoi, pour aller chercher des émotions ensemble .On peut et on doit aller encore plus loin dans l’investissement et dans la prise de conscience de nos possibilités. ».

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Sources indicate that team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

It has been revealed that “We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

This Just Giving page is a simple way for people, wherever they are in the world, to make a contribution to help rebuild these communities and bring some comfort to those who lost everything in the blink of an eye. Can Celtic boss Martin O'Neill muddle through until January cavalry arrives?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1278 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.

Since the first act of this season, a narrow win over Dundee, Martin O’Neill’s side have occupied a place of uncertainty.

Those who have taken the occasional stellar display to be indicative of a corner being turned have been left feeling like fools.

According to recent reports, there remain too many shortcomings in the squad, too many question marks hovering above too many players to ever feel that it has left inconsistency behind. The fan base has good reason not to quite trust it.

How could it be otherwise when the clean sheet claimed against bottom side Killie was the first in seven matches?

Kasper Hogh, the club’s record signing at £11million, hasn’t scored in his last 16 outings in green and white.

Martin O'Neill admits it has taken longer than he'd have liked for the new recruits to settle.

O’Neill’s options on the flanks include one player in Jota, who’s getting back from a long-term injury, and another in Yang Hyun-jun, who was recently sidelined for six weeks.

There’s a veteran in James Forrest, Seb Tounekti, not exactly the bravest of souls, and Haissem Hassan, a £6m signing who evidently believes defensive work is optional.

It indicates much that Callum Osmand, a centre-forward now trying to cut it on the flank, has become a fans’ favourite after just 13 senior appearances.

The concerns of the manager now extend to the middle of the park where Mika Baur may be out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

With Benjamin Nygren also a doubt to face St Mirren, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and/or Joel van den Berg could be teamed up with skipper Callum McGregor.

We’re assuredly about to discover if this squad has more about it than the results and performances to this stage have suggested.

‘We can make major improvements, there’s no question about it,’ stated the manager.

‘Top of the league, it is nice to be in that position. But other than a number of matches where I think we’ve played very, very well... maybe the Besiktas game, maybe the Hearts game, it’s been really hard work for us.

In a recent development, ‘That’s maybe a combination of things. Young and slightly more experienced players coming into the football club, getting to know the club, getting to know the players.

‘That’s taken a bit of time. I didn’t expect it to work immediately overnight.

German midfielder Mika Baur is set to miss around 10 weeks with an ankle ligament injury.

‘But they’re at a club where settling in is something they’ve got to do pretty rapidly.’.

Starting with the visit of the Paisley men, Celtic have 10 games up to and including the trip to Ibrox on January 3.

That encompasses two assignments on the road in the Europa League — Torreense and Omonia Nicosia.

O’Neill’s men also visit Tynecastle, Dens Park, Pittodrie and Tannadice in the league.

As they prepare to put up the Christmas decorations on the Celtic Way, O’Neill could privately be forgiven for wishing the festive season away.

January 5 is the day on which the transfer window in Scotland opens and you can’t help but wonder what Celtic’s prospects for the season will look like at that point.

While Camilo Duran and Baur have contributed, the bulk of the business done in the summer again looks to have been sub-standard.

To stand a chance of retaining the title, O’Neill badly needs several massive-hitters to come in without delay in the Upcoming Year.

‘We’re absolutely looking at players now,’ he stressed. ‘I suppose every single club is doing that. And the quicker you can get somebody in, the better.

It has been revealed that ‘We’ve seen when people are fit, we will have numbers. We just need a bit of quality.’.

Camilo Duran has been one of very few summer arrivals to have made an impact at Celtic.

Until such time as he can call for the cavalry, O’Neill has no choice but to make do and mend.

On the chances of prioritising the league and playing a weakened side in Europe, the veteran is clear.

Industry observers note that ‘Domestic football is really vital to the football club, of course,’ he stated. ‘But you’d still want to try and make some show in Europe. And we’ve found that difficult.

‘I genuinely thought against Besiktas we did really fine in the game, we didn’t over-press because they could play through you.

According to recent reports, ‘There are certain moments even in domestic football when teams can play through you. Kilmarnock caused us plenty of problems.

In a recent development, ‘I just think we’ve got to improve in the domestic games. We’ve got to be more aggressive in the sense of taking games to people and being less passive in periods of games.’.

O’Neill clearly needs more — much more — from so many individuals if he’s to get through the shark-infested waters of the next six weeks unscathed.

Hassan didn’t even make the matchday squad for Kilmarnock, a move which was interpreted by many as being a boot up the backside by a boss who’s been underwhelmed by his work without the ball.

‘We left out a number of players,’ O’Neill stressed. ‘I wouldn’t read as much into that, because a few will come back.

‘My job is not to please everyone, otherwise we’d have 26 players playing at one time.

O'Neill has backed misfiring striker Kasper Hogh to end his barren streak in front of goal.

‘I did a thing with corporate fans the other night, we had a bit of fun with some questions.

‘Apparently something came out that he [Hassan] was the most unpopular player in the dressing room, which is not true.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I didn’t say this. I was joking about my own unpopularity, as a player, because all I did was moan.

‘I did say about unpopularity, there’s at least one more unpopular. The crowd wanted to know but I didn’t tell them! I left it hanging. But it was tongue-in-cheek, apart from the part about me being unpopular, which I was.’.

The form of Hogh is no laughing matter. The Dane looked the part when he claimed a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, but that is beginning to feel like ancient history.

For his effort against the Ayrshiremen a fortnight ago to be ruled out for an earlier infringement by Baur was a low blow.

In a recent development, ‘For him, that was a killer,’ O’Neill reflected. ‘He has got the goal, gone off and celebrated and you just think... oh no, is that a goal?

Sources indicate that ‘He has worked exceptionally hard for us. But strikers live by goals and at some stage or other, he needs a goal.

‘The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net.

‘Shaun Maloney was telling me that for a little period he played up front when Henrik was injured for about a month.

‘And Henrik in that time was giving him advice about how centre-halves were reading him. He told him about getting yourself room, losing the centre-half, don’t be fighting with him all the time.

‘He scored a bag full of goals, so there must be something in it.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vous avez pu suivre la rencontre de cet après-midi en direct sur la chaîne YouTube de l'ASSE : à Aimé Jacquet, la réserve a logiquement battu 2-0 le Stade Beaucairois FC (lanterne rouge n'ayant pris que 2 petits points depuis le début de la saison de N2).

Dominateurs, les Verts ont péché dans la finition lors d'une première période qui a beaucoup penché à gauche avec l'association de deux joueurs dénichés à l'Institut Diambars (Sénégal) : le revenant Lassana Traoré (qui n'avait plus joué depuis 14 mois !) et le très prometteur ailier d'un an son cadet Etienne Mendy (photo), encore dans tous les bons coups ce dimanche. Ce dernier, à l'instar de Niels Rised, a eu l'occasion d'ouvrir le score en première période mais sa frappe trop écrasée a été arrêtée par le portier gardois. Suite à une énième percussion, il a délivré un centre parfait pour son capitaine Adam Baallal dont la tête n'a pas trouvé le cadre.

Industry observers note that deux minutes après le retour des vestiaires, les Verts ont fait sauter le verrou de Beaucaire sur un corner parfaitement tiré par Lucas Reynaud et repris magistralement par Mourtada Gueye d'une tête décroisée imparable. Obligés de courir après le score, les visiteurs ont laissé pas mal d'espace aux Verts, qui ont parfois confondu vitesse et précipitation au moment de porter l'estocade. Heureusement l'intenable Etienne Mendy a inscrit le but du break à la 82e d'un lob magistral de 47 mètres et Sainté a su parfaitement gérer la fin de match.

🙂‍↔️ Le lob de 50 mètres d'Étienne Mendy pour valider le succès de la Réserve ! https://t.co/P4pgjzieZI.

Les Verts consolident leur place sur le podium à 4 longueurs du leader Berre (battu par la réserve de l'OM) et à 3 points de l'Atlas Paillade, qui reste sur une série de 6 succès avant de recevoir l'ASSE lors de la prochaine journée, le samedi 5 décembre à 18h00. Une belle affiche en perspective à suivre sur Poteaux Carrés juste avant le choc au sommet de la 14e journée de L2 entre les leaders stéphanois et leurs dauphins nancéiens !

La compo : Colombet - Teillol, Gueye, Kasia, L.Traoré (Benkou, 46') - Depalle (A.Traoré, 69'), Baallal, Rised - Reynaud, Paalberg (Toty, 73'), E.Mendy.

La réaction de Sylvain Gibert :.

According to recent reports, "On est satisfait d'avoir enchaîné un 3e succès consécutif. C'était un math un peu piégeux au vu du classement de nos adversaires. J'avais donc mis en garde nos joueurs car Beaucaire avait perdu cette saison des matches qu'il ne méritait pas de perdre. J'avais vraiment alerté le groupe, lui avait demandé d'être rigoureux. On fait une bonne première demi-heure sans concrétiser, on a un peu déjoué le dernier quart d'heure de le première période, on a alors commis des fautes un peu bêtes, on a concédé des coups francs hereusement sans conséquence.

Industry observers note that le mot d'ordre à la mi-temps c'était de rester calmes, de continuer de jouer pour gagner à l'usure. Notre rapide ouverture du score en seconde période nous a facilité le travail. Je suis content qu'on ait ouvert le score sur coup de pied arrêté, on sait que ça permet parfois de décanter des matches. On bosse beaucoup là-dessus, Haïdar [Al-Shaïbani, entraîneur des gardiens, ndp2 et responsable des cpa, ndp2] en particulier. Le match a alors été plus ouvert car Beaucaire a dû un peu se découvrir pour tenter d'égaliser.

Etienne a fait parler son talent, il a mis un top but, un lob de près de 50 mètres du gauche alors que c'est un droitier. J'ai bien aimé l'état d'esprit des mecs, même à 2-0 on ne s'est pas relâché, on a continué d'attaquer et surtout de ne pas prendre de but. Cette victoire vient une fois de plus récompenser tout le boulot des joueurs. Vraiment, ça fait plaisir de coacher une vraie équipe, l'état d'esprit de tous les joueurs, notamment celui d'Adam qui a fait un très bon match au milieu. Tout le monde esst concerné, c'est appréciable !".

Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.

Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.

It has been revealed that adarabioyo began collecting as a child and returned to the hobby in 2020. His collection, which he shares on social media, spans a variety of sports and he also has several of Brazilian icon Neymar.

'I’ve been collecting for years, and it’s great to see the hobby continue to grow,' said the 29-year-old, who left Chelsea for Spurs last summer.

'I love collecting. It’s a great way for supporters to connect with their favourite players. I’ve always felt that collectors are some of the most passionate fans.

In a recent development, 'I’ve got to know so many collectors through the hobby. Talking about our collections is an instant icebreaker, and I know those conversations can mean a lot. I want to bring more players into the hobby and recreate those moments.

Tosin Adarabioyo, like many footballers, has a passion for collecting trading cards.

The latest shop is set to open in London's Borough Market next week.

Adarabioyo enjoyes collecting cards of former PSG star Neymar, who won 130 caps for Brazil.

'Neymar is criminally underrated to me, and I think his cards are too. Some of the images take me straight back to performances I’ve watched over the years. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like bottling up that feeling forever. Football purists will know what I mean.'.

West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, who played with Tosin at England youth level, is among backers along with James and Colwill.

Adarabioyo already has an online retail business, The Huddle, with guests such as Dominic Solanke, Robert Sanchez and Adam Wharton all featuring on live streams, opening boxes as fans watch.

Recent figures valued the global sports trading card market at $13.75billion (£10.5bn) in 2025, with that projected to grow to $27.52bn (£21bn) by 2034.

Formula One star Lewis Hamilton got in on the act earlier this year, launching his own venture and a shop in Frankfurt.

The seven-time world champion was already an ambassador for Topps - who also have the licence for Premier League cards - and noted: 'I’ve loved collecting cards since I was a kid — Pokemon, football, anything I could get my hands on.

According to recent reports, 'To now play a role in shaping the future of the category is incredible. We have a significant opportunity to tap into the culture in a way no one has before.'.

Industry observers note that pour son 4ème match en ligue 1 tunisienne, l'ancien Vert, Rayan Boukadida (19 ans) a inscrit son 1er but permettant à son club, l'US Monastir de l'emporter (2-0) sur l'Etoile Sportive du Sahel. Ce but, il l'a inscrit, comme souvent avec les équipes de jeunes de l'ASSE, de la tête suite à un coup-franc venu de la gauche. Il permet à l'US Monastir de grimper à la 4ème place, à 2 points du leader.

Rayan Boukadida, un enfant de Sainté, né à Saint-Etienne en 2007 a rejoint l'ASSE en 2013. Il avait 6 ans. Il a fait toute l'Ecole de Foot, toute la préformation chez les Verts. Il est entré au centre de formation en 2022, et n'a pas été conservé en 2025. Il a rejoint les rangs du Mans FC pour la saison 2025-2026, sa seule saison dans la cité mancelle car, le 2 août 2026, l'US Monastir, club de Ligue 1 tunisienne, a annoncé l'arrivée de l'ancien défenseur central vert. Rayan Boukadida rejoint donc un pays qu'il connaît bien puisqu'il compte 16 sélections dans les équipes U17 à U23 de Tunisie, en attendant mieux. Une belle opportunité pour lui certainement.

Le passage de Rayan Boukadida à l'ASSE n'est pas passé inaperçu car ce puissant défenseur central a la particularité d'avoir inscrit 18 buts en 4 saisons (de U15 à U19): - 2021-2022 : 4 buts avec les U15 de Jean-Philippe Primard- 2022-2023 : 3 buts avec les U17 Nationaux de Patrick Moreau- 2023-2024 : 5 buts avec les U17 de Frédéric Dugand- 2024-2025 : 6 buts avec les U19 de Frédéric Dugand.

#108104. Top five football betting tips and tricks

Top five football betting tips and tricks

📅 31 Aug 2018 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well.
  • According to recent reports, getting started on football betting is far from easy, though.
  • But experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

According to recent reports, getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

But experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having stated that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

It has been revealed that in this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it key to follow the action closely?

Industry observers note that first of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more vital, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

Sources indicate that as you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits.

Favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

In a recent development, if you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier mentioned than done, though.

Industry observers note that whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.
